reply_text:
I found one new 2010 prediction. I also met the three claims you already have, all in Shane Legg's own blog post of 10 December 2010.

- **Already recorded:** "Goodbye 2010" on vetta.org restates his human-level AGI forecast: a mean of 2028, a mode of 2025, and an upper bound of 2045 for the 90% range. It also says he chose to keep 2028 rather than bring it closer.
- **New:** in his "Summit 2010" post of 23 August 2010, he wrote that neuroscience "will be a major driving force behind AGI over the next 20 years."

Things I left out of the candidate list:

- **Undated:** the same August post says "I think AGI is approaching", with no date attached.
- **Not about AI:** the December post also says he is now "slightly more confident" there will be "a decent understanding of how cortex works before the end of the decade." That is a brain-science forecast, so it isn't a candidate. The post's supercomputer figure (10^18 FLOPS around 2018) is a hardware forecast, so it stays out as well.
- **No visible date:** a few of his blog comments do look forward with dates, but the pages I opened show no date on them. One is "late 2020's or early 2030's", replying under the December post. Another, "in 15-25 years" for hardware to simulate a brain, sits under a December 2009 post; search snippets dated his comments there to January 2010, but the page itself didn't show it. I've put these under other_years.
- **Not my words to quote:** two of the AI predictions came from a search snippet and the page wouldn't load past it. Rival forecasts in the comments are by other people.
- **Couldn't check:** one attendee's notes on the 2010 Singularity Summit cut off before the section on his talk. I also couldn't get a transcript of the 2010 AGI panel he sat on, so his spoken words that year are unchecked.
